name: ADDISON RES (SHAWN)

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front approach of the property, which consists of open desert scrubland terrain with scattered juniper and pine trees across a sandy, sloped hillside|No residence, driveway, or built structures are visible from this front perspective, indicating the structure sits well back from the front property boundary|The terrain slopes upward from the front and is densely vegetated with individual trees spaced throughout, which would limit direct foot approach and visibility toward the structure from this side.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the right side of the property from a low oblique angle, revealing a long, relatively flat to gently sloping desert terrain covered with scattered juniper-type trees and open sandy ground between them|No fencing, structures, driveways, or access routes are visible along the right side boundary|The open spacing between trees along this flank would allow foot movement but offers no improved vehicle access compared to the front.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, which is covered with the same desert scrub vegetation of scattered conifers on sandy terrain with a notable downward slope toward the rear|A small patch of green ground cover is visible near the upper-center of the rear area, which corresponds to the landscaped yard visible in the nadir near the residence|No rear vehicle access, fencing, or outbuildings are visible from this perspective.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property, presenting open sandy desert terrain with a dense scattering of juniper and pine trees across a sloping hillside|No structures, fencing, pathways, or access routes are visible along the left boundary|The terrain and vegetation pattern is consistent across all sides, indicating the property perimeter is open and unfenced throughout.

considerations: The residence sits on a large rural desert parcel accessed by a single curved paved driveway that connects to the road network to the northeast; this driveway is the only confirmed vehicle access route to the structure. The property is surrounded by open, unfenced desert scrubland with scattered juniper trees, which limits direct off-road vehicle approach but allows foot movement around the structure. A small paved turnaround area is visible adjacent to the residence in the nadir, providing limited on-site vehicle staging space. The long, curved driveway approach from the main road requires responders to navigate a winding path before reaching the structure.
clarifications: Is the driveway surface suitable for heavy emergency vehicles such as ladder trucks or heavy rescue units throughout its full length? Are there any locked gates or access control points along the driveway between the road and the residence? Does the property have a clearly marked address visible from the road at the driveway entrance? Are there any propane tanks, fuel storage, or other hazardous materials stored on the property not visible from aerial imagery?
